cardDescription: Clean and dry cold-weather footwear before putting it in storage.
focus: The setting is putting Winter Boots Away. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Outer bottom of a shoe that contacts the ground
Cord used to fasten a shoe
Container with a base and sides
Material made from treated animal hide
Wet soft earth beneath a pond visitor's boots
One of the year's familiar divisions, such as autumn

answerNotes.BOOT: A boot rises above the ankle. Its sole can leave a tread pattern in mud or snow.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.BRUSH: A brush holds many bristles in one handle. Their width and stiffness affect the marks or cleaning action it makes.
answerNotes.SOLE: The sole is the shoe's bottom. The tread is the pattern on its outer surface that contacts the ground.
answerNotes.LACE: A shoelace threads through openings to fasten a shoe. Lace can also name decorative openwork fabric, a different sense.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.

answerNotes.PAINT: Paint leaves a colored coating on a surface. A stain usually allows more of wood's natural grain to remain visible.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.BRUSH: A brush holds many bristles in one handle. Their width and stiffness affect the marks or cleaning action it makes.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.SAND: Sand consists of small loose grains. A pebble is much larger than an individual grain of sand.
answerNotes.STIR: Stir means move a utensil through a mixture. It combines ingredients without necessarily beating in much air.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.GLOVE: A glove has separate spaces for the fingers. A mitten groups the fingers together and has a separate space for the thumb.

words: Rubber-edged tool for clearing wet glass
Porous absorbent object used for wiping

One flat piece of glass in a window

answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.SOAP: Soap helps remove dirt when used with water. Rinsing carries away the loosened dirt and remaining suds.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.

answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.

focus: The setting is a Spring Door Basket of Twigs and Flowers. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Movable panel at a room's entrance

answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.HOOK: A fishing hook catches by its pointed curve. A wall hook is shaped for hanging objects rather than catching fish.
answerNotes.STEM: A stem supports leaves and flowers. It also connects the plant's growing parts with the roots below.
answerNotes.SPRING: Spring is the season between winter and summer. Weather and the exact timing of flowers vary by U.S. region.
answerNotes.NEST: A nest is a place for eggs and young. Many birds build nests, but the materials and locations differ from one species to another.
